tasks.short: Sell tickets and collect admission passes

steps.what: Clarify the patron's event, ticket type and access needs
Sell tickets, take payment and issue the selected admission
Collect presented admission tickets or passes at the entrance

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER}, the ticketing and point-of-sale system, to apply published tariffs, check capacity and issue the selected admission after payment. Keep the patron conversation, transaction confirmation and physical collection with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate tariff lookups and repeated selections slow attended sales.
tasks.enabler_now: An integrated ticketing till can combine selection, capacity, payment status and issuance.
tasks.still_hard: Concessions, accessible seating and payment problems require conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Help patrons select an appropriate admission and resolve confusing requests.
tasks.altitude: The attendant spends less time navigating sales screens; service and admission responsibilities stay the same.

reach.learn: Capacity controls, tariff effective dates and refund permissions

evidence.claim: Convious combines web, gate till and kiosk ticketing in one backend with cross-channel reporting.
The attended-sales navigation reduction is an E1 scenario; no customer self-service or physical collection saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary includes attended sales and physical collection. Authenticity examination belongs to task 5097; refusal belongs to task 5102 and is not included here.

The attendant produces event, quantity, ticket category and requested access details in s1 and s2; all capture remains within 30 full hours and 21 retained transaction hours. The box office supervisor supplies product ID, tariff version, concession rules and event capacity through existing product maintenance; changes needed for this design are counted as other-role upkeep.
Payment status comes from the existing payment terminal; unavailable or ambiguous status stops issuance for manual resolution in s2. No patron work is newly required.
Test native till configuration first. Existing automatic issuance and payment processing earn no saving; the scenario requires removable screen navigation.
unknowns: Existing till integration and navigation time
Availability of current capacity and concession rules
research_questions: Can an attended-sale trial reduce navigation while retaining selection capture and final confirmation?

already_counted.description: Patron clarification and transaction confirmation, capture and exceptions

incremental.description: Check failed sales and report configuration issues
Maintain ticket products and tariff mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact event, admission category, quantity, tariff, total and successful payment before issuance; changed details require confirmation again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+21+35=86; gross 14%, minus 3 focal upkeep gives 11% central net. Low assumes only six sales-navigation hours removed with the same upkeep. Patron effort and collection remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain order and enforce safety rules

steps.what: Observe the crowd and intervene to maintain order and safety

tasks.design: Keep crowd observation and safety intervention with venue staff. Existing rules in {DOCS} support training; no surveillance or automated enforcement system is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety depends on immediate physical conditions and people's responses.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change is needed for the proposed human workflow.
tasks.still_hard: A crowd can change faster than a record or alert can describe it.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise distress, communicate clearly and seek assistance at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Responsibilities and time allocation remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate assistance during a crowd incident

evidence.claim: Physical crowd observation and intervention retain their labour in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is the attendant's live crowd observation and intervention, excluding formal incident reporting and security officers' response.
No automated decision consumes structured crowd classifications; no new capture contract is required.
Existing training and rules remain in place. There is no new configuration or incremental upkeep, so zero new work is appropriate.
research_questions: Which crowd situations require additional trained staff?

incremental.description: No new system or workflow upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross saving and zero incremental upkeep. Physical safety work is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the presented ticket or pass and establish the event
Compare ticket details against admission validity criteria
Resolve authenticity exceptions and confirm the examination result

tasks.design: Configure deterministic validity checks in {OTHER}, the ticketing system, using ticket identifier, event, date, cancellation and prior-use status. Staff retain scanning or manual capture, inspect uncertain results and handle unreadable or unfamiliar passes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visual colours and dates require manual comparison and do not reliably reveal cancellation or prior use.
tasks.enabler_now: An issuance register supports fixed checks without interpreting patron behaviour.
tasks.still_hard: Unregistered legacy passes and offline operation need a human fallback.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an unreadable legitimate pass from a problem that needs escalation.
tasks.altitude: Less routine comparison; exception authority is unchanged.

reach.learn: Issuance history, cancellation status and offline limits

evidence.claim: Deterministic ticket checks can compare identifiers with an issuance register; the proposed scan-time and exception allowances are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is authenticity examination only. Sale, collection, final refusal and crowd management are assigned to their separate tasks.

The ticket attendant captures code, entrance event and unreadable status in s1, whose full 25 hours remain. The ticket issuing agent supplies unique ticket ID, event ID, valid dates, cancellation and prior-use status through the existing sale or entry transaction; this design adds no free upstream capture.
The entrance scan records prior use only after an accepted entry in the existing ticketing process; this task reads that status and does not claim its posting as saved labour.
Missing records, stale offline status or unreadable codes go to s3 manual examination. Native scanner and validity configuration must be tested before custom code.
research_questions: What fraction of currently manual comparisons can use the issuance register without more exception time?

already_counted.description: Ticket capture, result inspection and exception handling

incremental.description: Check scanner faults and validity-rule changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+15+25=65; gross 35%, minus 4 focal upkeep gives 31% central net. Low assumes just ten comparison hours removable because many passes remain visual. Existing scanner runtime itself earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Refuse admission when entry requirements are unmet

steps.what: Establish whether the person's entry meets objective venue requirements
Refuse admittance, explain the reason and request assistance if necessary

tasks.design: Staff apply the venue's objective entry rules and explain any refusal. Ticket evidence can come from {OTHER}, the ticketing system, but a failed scan alone does not make the refusal decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Refusal involves context, explanation and potential conflict.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing entry rules and ticket results already support the staff decision.
tasks.still_hard: A patron may have a legitimate explanation or need assistance.
tasks.human_edge: Apply rules consistently and de-escalate a difficult interaction.
tasks.altitude: Entry decision rights and refusal work remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Objective entry criteria and safe escalation

evidence.claim: Contextual admission refusal and de-escalation remain human work in this design.

assumptions: Boundary starts with the examination result from task 5097, whose producer and examination time belong there; do not repeat authenticity checks here.
No automated undesirability score or new structured classification is produced. Staff consider objective venue requirements and observed conduct.
No new system or process is introduced; incremental upkeep is zero. Test existing ticket result views before adding tools.
unknowns: Venue policy, escalation authority and accessibility arrangements
research_questions: Can staff explain each refusal using a clear entry requirement and offer an appropriate escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross saving and zero upkeep; no refusal conversation or contextual judgement is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce ticket screen navigation and routine comparisons while retaining patron service and safety decisions.
reach: Resolve disputed ticket records with the box office supervisor
role.ambitious_version: A venue attendant with more attention available for patrons who need help.
